----------------------------------------




INSIDE EVERY

IN WHICH DAN PLOTS TO CLONE US ALL

For years, Every CEO Dan Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9AZGFuc2hpcHBlciIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo3fQ==’s goal was to automate https://every. editor in chief Kate Lee https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0ZV8xNzY3IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjl9’s editorial judgment. The data was there—he had more than 30,000 of her historical edits—but the models weren’t good enough to create a copyediting agent that approached her abilities.

That changed with the launch of GPT-5.6 https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by92aWJlLWNoZWNrL2dwdC01LTYtc29sIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjEwfQ==. Now, before I file an article, I run it through KateBench, a skill that copyedits based on Kate’s historical edits. Only then does human Kate review the piece, accepting, modifying, or rejecting the agent’s suggestions. Tracked changes in Google Docs catalog those decisions and any additional edits she makes, then Codex rewrites the skill so it compounds. (For more on how KateBench works, read staff writer Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0aWUucGFycm90dDEyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjExfQ==’s writeup https://every. on how engineer Jannik Jung https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by90ZWFtIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjEzfQ== incorporates feedback to improve its performance.)

https://every. Kate copyediting agent makes suggested changes directly within the Google Doc. (All screenshots courtesy of the author.)




KateBench takes work off Kate’s plate. It also democratizes her expertise—anyone on the team can get a Kate-level quality pass for anything they’ve written. “It’s weirdly hard and specific to copyedit that well,” Dan says. “She’s the only one who can do it at her level, and now that’s not true anymore.”

https://every. self-improves by incorporating data on edits that were accepted versus rejected.




The obvious next step—at least if you’re Dan—is to build a version of KateBench for everyone at the company. That way, COO Brandon Gell https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIENhc2UgZm9yIENsb25pbmcgWW91ciBDb3dvcmtlcnMiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUyLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9AYnJhbmRvbl81MjYzIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjE2fQ==’s sharp user experience (UX) feedback, head of operations Arielle Shipper https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec

----------
howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy wednesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* OpenAI’s custom chip is beating Nvidia in early tests

* Anthropic thinks AI is a $30T market

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **VOICES**

## [Is your training data actually model-ready?](https://www.voices.com/solutions/audio-quality-whitepaper?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=client_audio-quality-whitepaper_2026)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/432154e1-1076-4b49-a0a9-863f6542d0cb/Newsletter_white_paper__1_.png?t=1787753343)
Follow image link: (https://www.voices.com/solutions/audio-quality-whitepaper?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=client_audio-quality-whitepaper_2026)
Caption: Courtesy: Voices

If you're fine-tuning a speech model, you've probably hit this wall: DNSMOS gives you a score, but it doesn't tell you whether the data behind that score is actually right for your model. Treat it as a pass/fail gate and you'll end up training on audio that looks clean on paper but drags down real-world performance while good source data gets tossed for no reason.

Voices' CTO DJ Jalali (with the team's senior audio and voice data engineers) just published a breakdown of the four-step calibration framework they use internally to set model-specific quality thresholds instead of trusting the raw DNSMOS number. It also covers where DNSMOS breaks down and how Voices validates audio for custom datasets at scale.

[Download the White Paper →](https://www.voices.com/solutions/audio-quality-whitepaper?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=client_audio-quality-whitepaper_2026)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e91b59e2-1333-438f-a248-4ae1fa9a4d41/OAIxBroadcom_1920x1080__1___1_.png?t=1787754409)
Caption: 

**1/ OpenAI’s custom chip is beating Nvidia in early tests** - OpenAI published the first benchmarks for [Jalapeño](https://openai.com/index/jalapeno-first-results/), its custom 700W inference chip built with Broadcom. In OpenAI’s [InferenceX tests](https://newsletter.semianalysis.com/p/openai-jalapeno-better-than-nvidia), it delivered 1.5–1.9x more AI work per watt and 1.7–3.6x lower end-to-end latency than Nvidia’s GB200 and GB300 systems across GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek R1 670B and Kimi K2.5 1T.

The interesting thing is OpenAI built it in just nine months, using its own models and Codex during development. It’s not trying to replace Nvidia either. OpenAI still needs Nvidia for training, and Jalapeño is mainly about making inference cheaper and faster.

Two more generations are already in the works, with Jalapeño starting to roll into OpenAI’s data centers later this year and ramping through 2027. So yeah, OpenAI is slowly becoming a chip company too.

Some interesting stuff related to this:

* Why is every AI lab [suddenly](https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenAI/comments/1uhn4y9/why_is_every_ai_lab_suddenly_trying_to_build/) trying to build their own chips?

**2/ Anthropic thinks AI is a $30T market** - Anthropic is [reportedly](https://www.pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/anthropic-readies-30-trillion-dollar-revenue-forecast-investors) telling IPO investors that its total addressable market is more than $30T, based on the amount of work AI models could theoretically do. That’s even bigger than SpaceX’s $28.5T TAM from its IPO filing.

Anthropic’s own numbers are a bit more interesting. Its revenue run rate has already passed $65B, and it’s projecting $190B-$200B in revenue for 2028.

Obviously, TAM numbers are mostly a way to tell investors “this can get really, really big.” But $30T is a pretty insane number. For context, the entire tech sector in the S&P 1500 made about $2.4T last year.

So either AI really is about to eat a huge chunk of the economy, or Anthropic has found the biggest TAM slide ever.


----------

----------
# TRENDING TOOLS


--------------------

* [OpenWorker](https://openworker.com/) - an open source agent that doesn't just chat but completes tasks on your laptop

BENCHMARKS DON’T KNOW YOUR JOB https://every.


PLUS: THE NUMBER KATEBENCH TAUGHT US TO COUNT, AND A SIX-AGENT SOLAR CREW HELPING DECIDE WHETHER TO RUN THE DRYER https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0aWUucGFycm90dDEyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjR9

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9hY2NvdW50IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjV9 to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



AI has a measurement problem. Companies know how much they spend on models and how those models score on public benchmarks. What they often don’t know is whether the models save employees time or produce work people can trust without rechecking. In today’s Context Window is a look at how companies can answer those questions for themselves: We explain why organizations need tests built around real work, show what cloning our editor in chief has taught Every about evals, and meet the six-agent crew helping an Every engineer decide whether his family can run the dryer.



----------------------------------------




SIGNAL

VIBES DON’T SCALE

Suppose your company is spending $100 million a year on AI. You know how much you’re paying—and you know where the models you’re paying for sit on the public leaderboards. But you may still have no idea whether they are doing the jobs you bought them for, or whether a cheaper model would do them just as well. This is a strange way to spend $100 million.

Mercor cofounder and CEO Brendan Foody says https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9CcmVuZGFuRm9vZHkvc3RhdHVzLzIwOTA1MDA5NDQ5NzkyNDMxODEiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6Nn0= he meets executives at companies in exactly this position: They spend as much as $100 million a year running models without “offline evals,” a fixed set of real tasks used to test and compare models before they touch live work. Box CEO Aaron Levie quote-posted Foody https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9sZXZpZS9zdGF0dXMvMjA5MTM1OTIyMzM2ODMxNTA1MCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo3fQ== with the line: “Enterprises will not be able to go just on vibes.”

Public benchmarks can tell you that one model is generally more capable than another. They can’t tell you whether it caught the clause your lawyers care about, preserved your house style, or spared an employee another round of checking. A useful eval starts with the work your company already does: representative cases, failures employees know to look for, and a count of what humans still have to fix.

Meanwhile, the number of plausible choices is multiplying. Investor Gavin Baker points to a chart https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9HYXZpblNCYWtlci9zdGF0dXMvMjA5MTU0MjAyNjA3MjMzODYyMyIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo4fQ== from Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch showing open-source models growing from 28 percent to 62 percent of token share on the frontend cloud platform in two months. Andreessen Horowitz’s charts of the week https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYTE2ei5uZXdzL3AvY2hhcnRzLW9mLXRoZS13ZWVrLXdpbmRzLW9mLXRoZW1hdGljIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjl9 report that legal workers have increased Codex adoption 108-fold since February. More models are becoming good enough for more work. Picking the highest-scoring one is no longer much of a buying strategy.

A reusable eval gives you a tool for determining whether a model can do your company’s work the way you want it done. Run the same set of tasks against each candidate, measure the work left for humans, and compare the savings. You can test a new model without starting from scratch or trusting the vendor’s favorite score.

At Every, we test each new model against the coding, writing, and knowledge-work tasks our team does every day in our Vibe Checks https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by92aWJlLWNoZWNrIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjEwfQ==. Now we’re going a step further: building internal evals that let us compare models over time, and see how wide the gap is between what a model does and what we need it to do. KateBench is an AI copyeditor trained on roughly 30,000 of editor in chief Kate Lee https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiQmVuY2htYXJrcyBEb27igJl0IEtub3cgWW91ciBKb2IiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUxLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0ZV8xNzY3IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjExfQ==’s past edits. It suggests changes in a Google Doc, then tracks which ones editors accept or reject, and what they still rewrite afterward. Evals help us determine how close the model’s judgments are to ones Kate might make.

howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy tuesday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

#### **VIKTOR**

Every model release makes AI smarter for free. The harness around the model decides how much of that turns into real work. A model that could do a great analyst's job is still stuck if it forgets everything between chats and only acts when someone types at it.

So we built Viktor for the models that are coming: a persistent workspace where it writes and runs code, memory that compounds across sessions, schedules it sets for itself, and 3,200+ tools it can call. The result is an AI employee in Slack and Microsoft Teams that runs work end to end. 60,000+ teams have hired one.

"I won't lie, when I first set it up... I was dubious. But wow... it's impressive." Simon Chapman, CTO

The full essay on our harness decisions is in the post.

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2bbde24c-ac2b-424a-b0d4-20df6780e533/World_SocialShare.width-1300__1_.png?t=1787670188)
Caption: Google’s Project Genie | World Model ==prototype==

**1/ Nvidia is taking its AI chips to space** - SpaceX is [building](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/spacexai-adopts-nvidia-vera-cpu-to-accelerate-agentic-ai-at-massive-scale) its Starmind orbital data centers around Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform, with a space version targeted for [Q4 next year](https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2091939113008238838?s=20). SpaceXAI is also using Nvidia’s Vera CPU for Grok’s agents.

The space version is apparently lighter, denser and cheaper, and built to deal with radiation and heat. Orbital compute costs 4x+ what it costs on Earth today, but Musk thinks that eventually flips.

Nvidia is also going after the CPU side of AI. [Vera](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/spacexai-adopts-nvidia-vera-cpu-to-accelerate-agentic-ai-at-massive-scale) is built to handle all the boring work around agents, like running code, calling tools, and moving data around, with Nvidia claiming up to 1.8x faster agentic task completion than traditional x86 chips.

So yeah, AI data centers might not all be on Earth forever.

**2/ AI is starting to move into the real world** - a bunch of new “[world models](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/ai-world-models-robotics-33ab46cb?st=xnEhg4&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink&utm_source=tldrnewsletter)” are being trained on videogames and simulations to control robots. Instead of learning what a cup is from text, they learn what happens when you actually move the thing.

General Intuition is one of the companies doing this. They’ve trained on millions of hours of videogame play, including the actions people take, and can apparently fine-tune the model to control a robot dog, drone or other machine.

Google DeepMind is already combining this with Gemini in [SIMA 2](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zphax4f6Rls&t=1s). Gemini handles the reasoning and goals, while SIMA learns to actually carry them out inside 3D game worlds.

And there is a _lot_ of money going into this. World Labs [raised $1B](https://www.worldlabs.ai/blog/funding-2026) at a $5.4B valuation, AMI Labs raised $1.03B at $3.5B, General Intuition [raised $133.7M](https://techcrunch.com/2025/10/16/general-intuition-lands-134m-seed-to-teach-agents-spatial-reasoning-using-video-game-clips/), Physical Intelligence [raised $600M](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-20/robotics-startup-physical-intelligence-valued-at-5-6-billion-in-new-funding) at $5.6B, and Wayve just [raised $1.2B](https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/24/self-driving-tech-startup-wayve-raises-1-2b-from-nvidia-uber-and-three-automakers/) at $8.6B. Google DeepMind is also pouring resources into SIMA, Genie and Veo, and Demis has said he expects world models to become an important part of Gemini’s planning.

The fun question is what happens when these things get plugged into LLMs. LLMs are pretty bad at understanding a 3D world, and you probably don’t want your robot hallucinating when it’s moving around.

Feels like we’re at the GPT-2 stage of physical AI.

More on world models:

* What’s [a world model?](https://blog.google/company-news/inside-google/googlers/ask-a-techspert/what-is-a-world-model-project-genie/)

* [The Waymo world model](https://waymo.com/blog/2026/02/the-waymo-world-model-a-new-frontier-for-autonomous-driving-simulation/) - a new frontier for autonomous driving simulation

# TRENDING TOOLS

A new lab says the sameness of AI prose is a training problem. It made the writing less predictable—but not necessarily any better.  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by93b3JraW5nLW92ZXJ0aW1lIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjF9


I TRIED THE AI MODEL BUILT TO FIX AI WRITING https://every.


A NEW LAB SAYS THE SAMENESS OF AI PROSE IS A TRAINING PROBLEM. IT MADE THE WRITING LESS PREDICTABLE—BUT NOT NECESSARILY ANY BETTER. https://every.

by Katie Parrott https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9Aa2F0aWUucGFycm90dDEyIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjR9

Midjourney/Every illustration.

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9ldmVyeS50by9hY2NvdW50IiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjV9 to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



Imagine a cover band that technically knows every song ever written but only has one arrangement. The melody consists of the same set of chords. The guitarist plays the same solo whether they are covering “Landslide” or “Party in the U.S.A.” By the fourth song, you are tired, and more than a little angry.

That’s what reading raw AI writing can feel like. The first few items you read, nothing trips your alarm—it’s just competent, if somewhat boring, writing. Then you keep seeing the same moves again and again: the patterns of three, the “not X, but Y,” the short sentence hanging off the back end of the paragraph that exists to do nothing but tell you that what you just read “matters.” Eventually you stop absorbing what the words are trying to communicate.

I’ve said before that it feels like model progress on writing at the major labs has stalled. Maybe no one model can be all things to all people, or maybe OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have bigger, more lucrative fish to fry in the coding space. On the one hand, fair enough. But as an AI-pilled writer, I can’t help feeling a little left out. It reminds me of high school, when the AP English paper deadline got pushed back after I’d already written it, because obviously the AP Physics exam took precedence.

So when I heard about a new, writing-focused model, I immediately queued it up for a Vibe Check.


WHAT IS DEFT?

Deft https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9kZWZ0d3JpdGluZy5jb20vIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjZ9 is a new research lab and model focused on “better writing.” The lab was cofounded by Justin Murphy https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9qbXJwaHkiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6N30=, a former political-science professor turned writer and publisher, and an AI researcher who goes by the name Rosmine https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiSSBUcmllZCB0aGUgQUkgTW9kZWwgQnVpbHQgdG8gRml4IEFJIFdyaXRpbmciLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0NDUwLCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwb3N0IiwidXJsIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly94LmNvbS9yb3NtaW5lIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjh9. Its first release, DFT v1, is a writing model post-trained with the lab’s custom fine-tuning method. Initially introduced in June, DFT v1 entered public beta last week.

The team behind Deft has a theory about why AI writing feels the way it does: LLMs have a distribution problem. Not in the sense of whether the writing gets read by people—it does, although not always happily. Deft is concerned with the distribution of the words themselves: which phrases recur, how sentences tend to begin and end, and whether a large body of output collapses toward the same handful of moves. The company’s bet is that, if you train a model to match the distribution of human writing across a batch of documents—not merely make each individual response acceptable—you’ll get prose with more range.

The engine driving Deft’s approach is a method called “distribution fine-tuning,” https://every. or DFT, a post-training step applied after a model has learned to predict language. Typical fine-tuning grades one response at a time, meaning that 1,000 responses can each pass inspection while in the aggregate, they are repeating the same openings and rhythms. DFT instead compares batches of model outputs with batches of human writing, then adjusts the model when the two distributions differ.

The resulting model is called DFT v1. On Deft’s tests, it produced a distribution of writing closer to the human samples than a conventional fine-tune of the same size. The basic claim is that changing the post-training will yield more range.

https://every. Deft console set to “rewrite” and “more human,” with the initial, AI-generated output provided. (All images courtesy of Katie Parrott.)




For now, the model is available via Deft’s website and paid API. You supply a prompt, choose whether you want the model to work faster, smarter, or “more human,” and choose an output format from a selection of four: news article, analytical essay, SEO article, or company blog. Advanced controls let you describe your writing sty

howdy, it’s Barsee again.

happy monday, AI family, and welcome back to AI Valley.

**here are the biggest things worth knowing today:**

* MIT researchers found AI can create “delusional spirals” 

* Humanoid robots are officially faster than Usain Bolt... kinda

* A mystery AI model is giving the frontier labs a headache

* Plus trending AI tools, posts, and resources

Let’s _dive_ into the Valley of AI…


----------

----------
#### **MOONSHOTS LIVE**

## [$2M to founders who used AI on a problem people have](https://moonshots.com/landing/ai-valley?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=mslive25&utm_content=2026-08-31)

Most of the futures we get shown are the ones falling apart. That is a failure of imagination with real consequences, because the futures we picture are the ones we end up building. So we put $5.5M behind the other kind.

The Build with Gemini XPRIZE gave builders 90 days to point AI at a problem people actually have. $2M across 25 winners, $500K to first, judged by Palmer Luckey, Cathie Wood, Anousheh Ansari, Mark Pincus and Logan Kilpatrick. Revenue was the proof it worked, not the point.

The same night a film gets greenlit for a $2.5M grant, chosen from 6,000 entries and judged by Neil deGrasse Tyson and Neal Stephenson.

More than 30,000 people competed. Everything is decided on one stage on September 25, in a restored 1920s movie palace in downtown LA. Nothing pre-recorded. 1,500 seats.

[Claim your seats](https://moonshots.com/landing/ai-valley?utm_source=ai-valley&utm_medium=newsletter&utm_campaign=mslive25&utm_content=2026-08-31)

~_*This is sponsored_~


----------

----------
#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/00caa63f-fa98-41e1-a1bd-b54d46ac07ea/-1x-1__3___1_.png?t=1787580698)
Caption: Courtesy: World Humanoid Robot Games

**1/ MIT researchers found AI can create “delusional spirals”** - they built a [mathematical model](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.19141) showing how a sycophantic AI can gradually make users more confident in a false belief by repeatedly validating it. And the weird part: making the AI more factual didn’t fully solve the problem. It could still cherry-pick true information that supported the user’s theory while ignoring evidence against it.

They also tried warning users that the AI might be flattering them... didn’t work. The belief spiral could still happen even when users knew about the AI’s tendency to agree with them. Basically, an AI doesn’t need to lie to reinforce a bad idea. It just needs to keep giving you the evidence you want to hear.

The paper points to a real risk, but it doesn’t mean every AI interaction will send you into a “delusional spiral.” A lot depends on how you use the model. If you configure it to challenge your assumptions, cite sources, and give you competing viewpoints, it can be much harder for this kind of spiral to happen. AI is already a great research tool and makes it much easier to automate repetitive work, but getting it to consistently challenge you and tell you when you’re wrong is still a very different problem.

**2/ Humanoid robots are officially faster than Usain Bolt... kinda** - a humanoid robot from Beijing-based X-Humanoid ran the [100m in 9.39 seconds](https://x.com/AP/status/2091451125786407202?s=20) at the [five-day](https://x.com/WHRGFUN) World Humanoid Robot Games, beating Bolt’s 9.58-second human record. The funny part is that braking was still a problem... some robots basically [crashed](https://x.com/AP/status/2091451125786407202?s=20) into the mat after crossing the finish line. [Another robot](https://x.com/MarioNawfal/status/2091558583683232242?s=20) cleared 2.88m in the standing high jump, also above the human record. More than 2,000 robots are competing across 51 events, including [jumping](https://x.com/ViralRushX/status/2091811768364605512?s=20), soccer, [table tennis](https://x.com/kyleichan/status/2091271208234836178?s=20), [ping-pong](https://x.com/MarioNawfal/status/2091568649802789247?s=20), and weightlifting.

There’s a catch, though... These robots aren’t exactly ready to replace Olympic athletes or humans at work. Humanoids are still mostly being used for research and demonstrations, but the rapid improvement is pretty wild. China is also producing the majority of the world’s humanoid robots, making these games another showcase in the growing US-China robotics race.

**3/ A mystery AI model is giving the frontier labs a headache** - a stealth model called [Ox Alpha](https://openrouter.ai/stealth/ox-alpha) appeared on OpenRouter from an anonymous provider and quickly started going viral among developers. It’s built for coding and long-running agentic work, with a 1.05M-token context window, 131K-token outputs, and reportedly enough capacity to process 100T tokens per day.

Early tests suggest [Ox Alpha](https://x.com/OpenRouter/status/2090544970923184269?s=20) may be beating models like Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on coding benchmarks such as Deep SWE... although there’s no independent validation on public leaderboards yet. Stripe CEO Patrick Collison called it “very impressive,” which probably didn’t help calm the speculation around who actually built it.

And everyone is trying to figure out who’s behind it. The guesses range from Google’s next Gemini to Microsoft’s MAI models to Chinese labs like Z.ai. Nothing has been confirmed.
